title: policy.json: dispatch
description: Sizing ready items into tiers, the brief, and the dispatch plan (design parts 5.1 and 5.2). The tiers themselves (executor, model class, effort) are in the tiers section.

inline_globs.description: Paths the orchestrator edits itself (tier 0): an item whose touches all fall here, such as a tracker edit, is not dispatched.

sensitive_globs.description: Paths whose change raises an item one tier for blast radius: the build and release pipeline, dependency manifests, security-sensitive code, the project's own policy.

owner_review_areas.description: Areas whose output the owner reviews in person, such as UI: their items go to tier 3, their own session.

tier1_max_touches.description: The most touches globs an item may list and still be tier 1 (mechanical, fully specified work).

familiar_min_yield.description: Down one tier for familiar ground: the share of first-pass successes the lower tier must have had on this area and item kind.

familiar_min_samples.description: How many past dispatches at the lower tier, in the same area and kind, before familiar ground counts.

default_estimates.description: The token estimate per tier when no similar item has been done before. Replaced by the median of similar past items once there are some.

report_at_budget_multiple.description: The brief asks the executor to report at this multiple of its token budget, even if unfinished.

serialize_overlap_share.description: Hold an item back while running items already cover at least this share of its touches globs. Below it, overlapping items run in parallel and the later one rebases.

tier3_mode.description: How a tier-3 item runs by default: headless (a background claude -p run in its own worktree; its exit is the completion notice) or interactive (a session the owner starts and steers).

headless_permission_mode.description: The permission mode a headless tier-3 run starts in. The project's own allow and deny rules still apply.

brief_kb.description: Knowledge-base pages a brief points to, per area: page paths with an optional #section.
